name: Fertiliser supply
summary: Egyptian urea cleared near $535 a tonne for November, up 17% since September after gas supply to some plants was cut
state: Egyptian granular urea for November contracts cleared at about $535 a tonne FOB, up about 17% from $457 in September, after producer Kima reported a 20% cut in its gas supply from 1 Nov (Fertilizer Daily, 9 Nov). Egypt is now the priciest of comparable export origins. No rise of 60% in three months was found and the Hormuz route remains impeded rather than closed, so the Alert is unconfirmed and Watch holds as of 11 Nov.
for_you: Fertiliser costs feed into farm budgets for next season's crops and, over time, into food prices. Arable farmers buying nitrogen for spring applications are most exposed.
rubric_hit: Gulf export route impeded with Egyptian supply cuts; urea +17% since Sep, below +60% Alert line

sources.title: Fertilizer Daily — Egyptian urea price rises as gas supply is cut

why: Fertiliser prices lead food prices by months; much of the world's urea and ammonia is exported from Russia, the Gulf and China.
drivers: Gas prices, Gulf shipping, export bans and quotas, sanctions, planting seasons.

rubric.alert: Urea up more than 60% in three months, several major exporters restricting at once, or a key export route closed.
rubric.watch: Urea up more than 30% in three months, or a major exporter restricts exports.
rubric.normal: Urea and ammonia prices within their normal range; no major export restrictions.
